purpose: Domain knowledge for LLM-based OEE Loss Analysis & Improvement Agent. Maps standardized downtime error codes (DT-00 to DT-08) to manufacturing engineering context: causes, symptoms, OEE impact, and maintenance response.
taxonomy_note: DT-00 to DT-08 are mapped to the standard TPM Six Big Losses framework plus baseline running state and planned downtime, ensuring full coverage of Availability, Performance, and Quality loss categories.

error_codes.category: Baseline Productive Time (No Loss / Running State)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Represents time during which equipment is running at or near ideal cycle time, producing conforming product, with no active loss event. This is the reference state against which all six big losses are measured.
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Contributes positively to Availability, Performance, and Quality simultaneously; drives OEE toward target.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: None — counted as fully productive run time.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: None — cycle time tracking at or near 100% of ideal cycle time.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: None — output within specification, no scrap/rework generated.
common_machine_symptoms: Stable, repeating cycle time
Output count tracking linearly with takt time
No active alarms or fault codes
Consistent process parameters (pressure, temperature, torque, feed) within control limits
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: 0 minutes (not a downtime-generating code; used as the OEE calculation baseline)
common_diagnostic_checks: Cycle time trend vs. ideal/standard cycle time
Output count reconciliation against planned production time
SPC control chart review for early drift detection
error_codes.production_consequences: None — this is the target operating state; sustained DT-00 time is the objective of loss elimination efforts.
error_codes.business_consequences: Meets production plan, supports on-time delivery (OTD), maximizes throughput per labor and asset hour.
common_maintenance_actions: Log baseline performance data for trend and capability analysis
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Passive monitoring via CMMS/SCADA
Use baseline data to calibrate PM intervals and OEE targets

error_codes.category: Breakdown Loss — Unplanned Mechanical Failure (Six Big Loss #1)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Unplanned stoppage caused by failure of a mechanical component (bearing, belt, gearbox, seal, tooling, structural element) that halts production until repaired. The most severe and costly category of Availability loss.
typical_equipment_involved: Press Line (clutch-brake, ram guides, hydraulic power unit)
CNC Milling (spindle bearings, ball screws, way covers)
Assembly Line (conveyor drives, gearboxes, pneumatic actuators)
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Severe, immediate Availability loss; frequently cascades into Performance loss (restart ramp-up) and Quality loss (startup scrap).
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: High — direct unplanned run-time loss, typically 30 minutes to 8+ hours depending on component and spare parts availability.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: Indirect — post-repair restart often runs below rated speed until process stabilizes.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: Indirect — first parts after restart may be out of tolerance due to thermal/mechanical re-settling.
common_machine_symptoms: Sudden, unexpected stop with hard fault indication
Abnormal noise, vibration, or heat prior to failure (often missed if not monitored)
Loss of hydraulic or pneumatic pressure
Visible component damage (broken belt, sheared key, cracked casting)
Burning smell or smoke from motor/gearbox
possible_operational_causes: Operating beyond rated capacity/tonnage/load
Deferred or skipped preventive maintenance
Foreign object damage (FOD) introduced into equipment
Operator override of safety interlocks or load limits
possible_mechanical_causes: Bearing failure due to lubrication breakdown or contamination
Belt or chain breakage from fatigue or misalignment
Seal/gasket failure causing fluid loss
Tooling or die breakage from fatigue cracking
Gearbox failure (gear tooth wear, shaft misalignment)
possible_electrical_causes: Motor overload trip due to mechanical binding
Contactor or relay failure preventing restart
Safety interlock/sensor fault forcing emergency stop
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: 30–480 minutes depending on failure severity and spare parts availability
common_diagnostic_checks: Vibration analysis on rotating equipment
Thermal imaging of motors, bearings, and electrical panels
Oil/lubricant analysis for contamination or metal particulate
Visual inspection of wear components (belts, seals, tooling edges)
Fault/error log review on machine controller
error_codes.production_consequences: Full line stoppage, missed takt, downstream station starvation, potential upstream line back-up if buffer capacity is exceeded.
error_codes.business_consequences: Missed on-time delivery (OTD), overtime/expedite costs, expedited spare parts freight, potential customer escalation.
common_maintenance_actions: Update PM plan/interval based on failure mode
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Dispatch technician immediately (emergency work order)
Pull spare parts from crib/inventory
Document RCFA in CMMS
Update FMEA and PM schedule based on failure mode found

error_codes.category: Breakdown Loss — Electrical / Control System Fault (Six Big Loss #1, electrical subtype)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Stoppage caused by electrical, PLC, servo drive, sensor, or HMI malfunction rather than a mechanical component failure. Often presents as intermittent nuisance faults that are harder to diagnose than mechanical breakdowns.
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: High Availability loss for hard faults; repeated short Availability losses for intermittent/nuisance faults that can mimic small-stop patterns.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: High for hard faults (E-stop, drive fault); moderate but chronic for intermittent faults.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: Low to moderate if the fault forces a reduced-speed fallback mode.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: Low to moderate if sensor drift causes a miscalibrated process parameter before detection.
common_machine_symptoms: Fault code displayed on HMI/operator panel
Unexpected E-stop trips with no visible mechanical cause
Communication loss between PLC and drives/sensors
Servo drive alarm (overcurrent, following error, encoder fault)
Intermittent resets that clear themselves
possible_operational_causes: Incorrect parameter entry by operator or setup technician
Unauthorized parameter override
Electromagnetic interference (EMI) from nearby equipment
possible_mechanical_causes: Loose wiring/connectors caused by machine vibration
Connector corrosion in harsh environments (coolant, humidity)
possible_electrical_causes: Sensor (proximity, photo-eye, limit switch) failure or drift
PLC I/O card failure
Power supply voltage fluctuation or sag
Encoder/resolver failure
Servo drive fault
Grounding/bonding issue causing noise on signal lines
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: 10–240 minutes; can recur multiple times per shift if intermittent
common_diagnostic_checks: PLC/drive fault log export and review
Continuity and insulation resistance testing on suspect wiring
Sensor calibration and alignment check
Power quality analysis (voltage sag, harmonics)
I/O forcing/simulation test to isolate faulty input/output
error_codes.production_consequences: Intermittent, unpredictable stoppages that are difficult to schedule around; erodes operator trust in equipment reliability.
error_codes.business_consequences: Controls engineering support cost, risk of latent recurring faults that resist first-pass repair, potential for repeat visits.
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Dispatch controls/electrical technician
Export and analyze fault history log
Recalibrate or replace sensors
Review recent software/firmware changes for regression

error_codes.category: Setup and Adjustment Loss (Six Big Loss #2)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Downtime associated with changing over tooling, dies, molds, fixtures, or programs between product runs, including first-piece trial and adjustment. Planned in nature but frequently exceeds standard due to lack of standardized work.
typical_equipment_involved: Assembly Line (fixture and program change for model changeover)
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Direct Availability loss (counted against run time unless the OEE model explicitly excludes changeover from Planned Production Time).
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: Moderate to high; scheduled but highly variable in duration based on operator skill and standardization.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: Low, unless the post-changeover adjustment phase runs at reduced speed before full-rate confirmation.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: Moderate — first-off parts during trial/adjustment are frequently out of specification.
common_machine_symptoms: Extended idle time between last-good part of prior run and first-good part of new run
Repeated trial cycles with manual jogging/adjustment
Operator searching for tools, fixtures, or setup documentation
Multiple first-article inspection rejections before acceptance
possible_operational_causes: No standardized changeover procedure (no SMED/quick-changeover standard work)
Tools, dies, or fixtures not staged at point of use
Incorrect or missing setup documentation/recipe
Inexperienced or undertrained operator performing changeover
possible_mechanical_causes: Worn locating pins, clamps, or datums requiring repeated realignment
Die/mold wear requiring shimming or manual compensation
possible_electrical_causes: Slow program upload/download to controller
Incorrect recipe/program selected from library
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: 15–180 minutes depending on product complexity and changeover standardization maturity
common_diagnostic_checks: Changeover time study with internal vs. external step classification (SMED analysis)
Tooling/fixture condition and calibration check
Setup documentation accuracy audit
error_codes.production_consequences: Reduced available run time; creates pressure toward larger batch sizes to amortize changeover cost, increasing WIP and inventory.
error_codes.business_consequences: Reduced manufacturing flexibility, higher inventory carrying cost, schedule adherence risk on high-mix product lines.
common_maintenance_actions: Development of standardized changeover kits and staged tool carts
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Ensure tooling/fixture readiness and PM prior to scheduled changeover
PM on quick-change mechanisms (clamps, locators, quick-disconnects)
Participate in SMED kaizen events to reduce internal setup steps

error_codes.category: Small Stops / Idling Loss (Six Big Loss #3)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Brief stoppages, typically under 5–10 minutes, that do not require formal maintenance intervention and are often self-cleared by the operator (jams, misfeeds, blocked sensors, minor misalignment). Individually minor but cumulatively one of the largest and most under-reported OEE losses.
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Depresses both Availability (frequent micro-stoppages) and Performance (net effective rate falls well below rated speed); commonly underreported in manual data collection systems.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: Low-to-moderate per event; high cumulative impact due to frequency (often 10–50+ events per shift).
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: Moderate to high — the dominant driver of chronic Performance loss on high-speed automated lines.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: Low direct impact, but misfeeds and jam-clearing can induce downstream defects.
common_machine_symptoms: Frequent short-duration alarms (seconds to a few minutes)
Part jams at transfer or infeed/outfeed points
Photo-eye or proximity sensor repeatedly blocked/triggered
Operator repeatedly clearing jams and pressing reset without logging a formal stop
possible_operational_causes: Inconsistent upstream component supply (starvation/blocking)
Poor operator technique during manual loading
Incoming material/component dimensional variability
possible_mechanical_causes: Misaligned guide rails or transfer fingers
Worn feed mechanism (belts, chains, star wheels)
Chain or belt tension out of specification
possible_electrical_causes: Sensor sensitivity/threshold misadjustment
Debris or glare interfering with optical sensors
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: 1–10 minutes per event; high frequency makes cumulative daily impact substantial
common_diagnostic_checks: Pareto analysis of stop reason and frequency by station/asset
Sensor alignment and sensitivity verification
Feed mechanism physical inspection
Video/motion analysis at chronic jam points
error_codes.production_consequences: Chronic underperformance relative to rated line speed; difficult to capture accurately without automated stop-detection, leading to underestimated true capacity loss.
error_codes.business_consequences: Hidden capacity loss — often the single largest unrecognized contributor to OEE gap; increases operator fatigue and reduces trust in line reliability.
common_maintenance_actions: Enable and support autonomous maintenance (operator-led cleaning, inspection, lubrication)
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Trend micro-stop frequency by station using SCADA/MES data
Support and audit autonomous maintenance program compliance
Adjust sensor thresholds and perform targeted precision maintenance

error_codes.manufacturing_description: Equipment running below its designed ideal cycle time or rated speed without a hard stop, typically due to operator caution, mechanical wear, or deliberate process derating. Directly reduces the Performance factor of OEE.
typical_equipment_involved: CNC Milling (feed rate override reduced below 100%)
Assembly Line (conveyor/line speed reduced below design takt)
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Direct Performance loss; Performance = (Ideal Cycle Time × Output Count) / Run Time falls below 100% even though the machine never stops.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: None to low — the machine is running and generating output.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: High — this is the primary loss category this code represents.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: Low to moderate — sometimes speed is deliberately reduced to protect quality; other times wear-induced defects appear despite the slower rate.
common_machine_symptoms: Actual cycle time consistently exceeds standard/ideal cycle time
Feed rate or speed override set below 100% on controller
Throughput trending below rated capacity with no stoppage recorded
Motor current/load below expected value at reduced feed
possible_operational_causes: Operator running below standard rate for comfort or perceived risk avoidance
Inaccurate or outdated standard cycle time reference
Inadequate operator training on rated capability
Deliberate derate to reduce scrap risk (informal compensation for an unaddressed root cause)
possible_mechanical_causes: Tooling wear increasing cutting/forming resistance
Worn bearings or guides increasing friction
Hydraulic system pressure drop limiting cycle speed
Inadequate lubrication increasing mechanical drag
possible_electrical_causes: Servo/drive parameter drift from optimal tuning
Degraded servo tuning causing conservative acceleration limits
VFD thermal derating due to overheating or duty cycle limits
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: Not applicable — continuous rate loss rather than a discrete stoppage; quantified as lost-production-equivalent minutes
common_diagnostic_checks: Cycle time trend analysis vs. engineered standard
Feed/speed override log review over time
Tooling wear inspection and replacement interval audit
Motor load/current analysis at constant commanded feed
error_codes.production_consequences: Chronic shortfall against planned output; frequently requires overtime or extended shifts to recover volume.
error_codes.business_consequences: Hidden capacity loss — frequently the largest unrecognized OEE gap in a facility; increases per-unit manufacturing cost.
common_maintenance_actions: Joint re-validation of standard cycle time with process/industrial engineering
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Capture and compare actual vs. ideal cycle time from controller data
Investigate mechanical drag sources (bearings, guides, hydraulics)
Coordinate with process/industrial engineering on rate standard validation

error_codes.category: Startup / Yield Loss (Six Big Loss #6 — Reduced Yield)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Defective parts produced during machine warm-up, post-changeover startup, or process stabilization before the process reaches steady-state quality capability. Distinct from in-process running defects (DT-07).
typical_equipment_involved: CNC Milling (thermal growth affecting first-part accuracy)
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Direct Quality loss concentrated at the start of a production run.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: None direct — the machine is running.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: Low — may include slower initial cycles during controlled ramp-up.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: High — direct scrap/rework concentrated in the first parts of a run.
common_machine_symptoms: First N parts out of dimensional or visual tolerance
Dimensional drift observable during the warm-up window
Process parameters (temperature, pressure) not yet stabilized against target
Repeated first-article inspection failures before acceptance
possible_operational_causes: Inadequate or skipped warm-up procedure
First-article inspection skipped or rushed to meet schedule pressure
Production restarted immediately after changeover without stabilization dwell
possible_mechanical_causes: Thermal expansion of tooling, spindle, or die not yet stabilized
Die/mold temperature not at process setpoint
Hydraulic oil viscosity/temperature affecting initial cycle consistency
possible_electrical_causes: Incorrect initial process parameters loaded from recipe
Sensor calibration drift specific to cold-start conditions
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: Not applicable — a yield loss, typically manifesting across the first 5–50 parts of a run
common_diagnostic_checks: SPC chart review isolating startup-window parts
Thermal stabilization time study (time-to-target-temperature)
First-article inspection record review across multiple changeovers
error_codes.production_consequences: Recurring scrap/rework at the start of every production run, disproportionately costly on lines with frequent changeovers.
error_codes.business_consequences: Material waste cost, effectively inflates the true cost of each changeover beyond the recorded DT-03 downtime.
common_maintenance_actions: Standardize and enforce warm-up cycle duration
Install/maintain preheating systems (mold/die heaters, spindle warm-up cycles)
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Verify heating/cooling system function ahead of scheduled changeovers
Support and audit warm-up SOP compliance
Calibrate sensors specifically involved in startup process control

error_codes.category: Quality Defects / Rework Loss (Six Big Loss #5 — In-Process Running Defects)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Non-conforming product produced during normal steady-state running (not during startup), requiring scrap or rework. Distinct from DT-06 in that the process was previously stable and has since drifted or been disturbed.
typical_equipment_involved: All equipment types — Press Line, CNC Milling, Assembly Line
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Direct Quality loss occurring mid-run, often signaling tooling wear or process drift rather than a startup condition.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: None direct, unless the line is stopped for containment or quality hold.
error_codes.expected_performance_impact: Low — rework may consume additional cycles or station time.
error_codes.expected_quality_impact: High — direct impact on First Pass Yield (FPY) and scrap rate.
common_machine_symptoms: SPC out-of-control signals (points beyond control limits, trends, runs)
Dimensional drift accumulating over the course of a run
Visual defects (burrs, scratches, flash, surface finish degradation)
Functional/torque/leak test failures
possible_operational_causes: Incoming material lot-to-lot variation
Operator error or deviation from work instructions
Inadequate or unclear standard work instructions
Tooling wear that has not yet triggered a wear-limit alarm
possible_mechanical_causes: Tool or die wear progressing through the run
Worn locating features causing positional drift
Misalignment developing over run duration (thermal or vibration-induced)
possible_electrical_causes: Process sensor drift (pressure, temperature, torque transducers)
Closed-loop control parameter drift not caught by existing control limits
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: Not applicable — a continuous quality loss quantified as a defect rate percentage rather than a stoppage duration
common_diagnostic_checks: SPC control chart review for trend/shift patterns
Defect Pareto analysis by defect type and location
Tooling wear inspection against wear-limit specification
Incoming material certificate/lot review
Torque, pressure, or temperature trend review against process window
error_codes.production_consequences: Direct scrap cost, added rework labor, potential containment sort or quality hold on downstream/finished goods inventory.
error_codes.business_consequences: Customer complaint and PPM impact, warranty exposure, potential line-side sorting or 100% inspection cost.
common_maintenance_actions: Tooling replacement or refurbishment on defined wear intervals
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Execute tooling PM on defined interval
Calibrate process and quality sensors
Support SPC root-cause investigation jointly with quality engineering
Coordinate containment actions with quality department

error_codes.category: Planned Downtime (Excluded from OEE; affects TEEP)
error_codes.manufacturing_description: Scheduled stoppage for planned maintenance, scheduled breaks, shift changes, or periods with no production demand. Standard OEE calculations exclude this time from the Planned Production Time base; it is captured separately to compute Total Effective Equipment Performance (TEEP).
error_codes.expected_oee_behaviour: Excluded from the OEE calculation base under standard methodology; reduces TEEP, not OEE.
error_codes.expected_availability_impact: None to OEE Availability (excluded from denominator); reduces calendar-time utilization (TEEP).
common_machine_symptoms: Machine intentionally offline per production schedule — not a fault condition
No alarms; controller in standby/off state
possible_operational_causes: Gap in production schedule (no orders/no demand)
Scheduled shift break or shift change
Scheduled preventive maintenance window
No material available for a scheduled production block
error_codes.typical_downtime_range: Scheduled duration — typically 15–60 minutes for breaks, 2–8 hours for PM windows
common_diagnostic_checks: PM compliance rate review (completed on schedule vs. missed)
Planned vs. actual PM duration variance analysis
Overrun tracking — instances where DT-08 extends into scheduled production time
error_codes.production_consequences: None if properly scheduled and executed within window; risk arises only if the PM window overruns into planned production time, which then should be reclassified as an Availability loss (DT-01/DT-02 pattern).
error_codes.business_consequences: Direct PM labor/parts cost, but reduces future unplanned breakdown risk (DT-01) when PM scope is executed effectively.
common_maintenance_actions: Execute PM checklist per asset PM plan
Planned component replacement per wear-life schedule
error_codes.severity: Low (as planned); escalates to High if it overruns into production time
typical_maintenance_department_actions: Execute PM tasks per schedule and document completion in CMMS
Update PM intervals/scope based on findings during the window
Track PM window adherence as a maintenance KPI
